slides.title: Exam question [3]
slides.oldHtml:
Exam question [3]

Explain what happens in the muscles when you exercise at a high intensity.
3 marks
Mark scheme — individual marking pointsAny 3 of 5 = full marks [3]
✓Heart and lungs cannot supply enough oxygen to the muscles fast enough[1]
✓Less aerobic respiration occurs (so less ATP / energy is released)[1]
✓Muscles switch to anaerobic respiration (glucose → lactic acid)[1]
✓Lactic acid builds up in the muscle cells[1]
✓Causes muscle fatigue / cramp (and creates an oxygen debt)[1]
Command word: EXPLAIN
Link each step with so / because — aim for 3+ distinct scientific points.
slides.newHtml:
Exam question [3]

Explain what happens in the muscles when you exercise at a high intensity.
3 marks
Mark scheme — linked chain (EXPLAIN)Any 3 linked points (max 3)
1Heart & lungs cannot supply enough oxygen to muscles fast enough[1]
↓so…
2Less aerobic respiration occurs (and less ATP / energy is released)[1]
↓therefore…
3Muscles switch to anaerobic respiration (glucose → lactic acid)[1]
↓which causes…
4Lactic acid builds up in muscle cells[1]
↓leading to…
5Muscle fatigue / cramp (and an oxygen debt repaid afterwards)[1]
EXPLAIN = linked chain
Connect each step (so / therefore) — and say energy is released, never "made".

slides.oldHtml:
Evaporation

Liquid → gas without boiling
  • Fastest particles escape from the surface
  • Happens at any temperature below the boiling point
  • Boiling forms bubbles throughout the liquid at the boiling point

slides.title: Do covalent substances conduct?
slides.oldHtml:
Do covalent substances conduct?

Usually no
  • Molecules have no overall charge
  • No mobile ions or free electrons
  • Exception: graphite (delocalised e⁻)
  • Click substances to test!

slides.title: Weight: example & your turn
slides.newHtml:
Weight: example & your turn

Worked example (FIFA)
An astronaut has mass 80 kg on Mars (g = 3.8 N/kg). Calculate her weight.
F: W = m × g
I: W = 80 × 3.8
A: W = 304 N
Your turn (whiteboards)
1. Same astronaut on Jupiter (g = 26 N/kg).
→ W = 80 × 26 = 2080 N
2. A rover weighs 760 N on Mars (g = 3.8 N/kg). Find its mass.
→ m = W ÷ g = 760 ÷ 3.8 = 200 kg
3. What is the rover’s mass on Earth?
→ Still 200 kg (mass never changes!)

slides.title: Orbital speed: watch the units
slides.oldHtml:
Orbital speed: watch the units

orbital speed=2 × π × orbital radiustime period
Distance in m and time in s → speed in m/s
Distance in km and time in days → speed in km/day
slides.newHtml:

orbital speed=2 × π × orbital radiustime period
SI units → m/s
r in m, T in s
Distance
km → m: × 1000

slides.title: Worked example: Mercury
slides.oldHtml:
Worked example: Mercury

QUESTION: Mercury takes 87.97 days to orbit the Sun. Orbital radius = 57.91 million km. Find its orbital speed.
Step 1 — One orbit distance (2πr)
2 × π × 57.91 million km = 363.9 million km
Step 2 — Divide by time period (T)
363.9 million ÷ 87.97 = 4.14 million km/day
Step 3 — Convert to m/s (1 day = 86 400 s)
4 140 000 000 m ÷ 86 400 s = 47 900 m/s
slides.newHtml:
Worked example: Mercury

QUESTION: Mercury orbits the Sun in 87.97 days with orbital radius 57.91 million km. Calculate its orbital speed in m/s (3 s.f.).
F — Formula & convert to SI units first
v = 2πr ÷ T  |  r = 5.791 × 1010 m  |  T = 87.97 × 86 400 = 7 600 608 s
I — Insert values into the formula
v = (2 × π × 5.791 × 1010) ÷ 7 600 608
F / A — Fine-tune & Answer with units
v = 47 900 m/s (or 4.14 million km/day)

slides.title: Whiteboards: orbital speed
slides.newHtml:
Whiteboards: orbital speed

Your turn (FIFA): solve 1 → 3 in order on your whiteboard, then click to checkv = 2πr ÷ T
1. Direct SI: A rock on a string swings in a circle of radius 1.2 m. One turn takes 0.5 s. Find its speed.
→ v = 2 × π × 1.2 ÷ 0.5 = 15.1 m/s
2. Convert units: The Moon orbits Earth in 27 days with orbital radius 362 600 km. Find its speed in m/s.
→ v = (2 × π × 362 600 000) ÷ (27 × 86 400) = 977 m/s (84 400 km/day)
3. Rearrange challenge: A satellite orbits at 7500 m/s with radius 7 000 000 m. Find its time period T.
→ T = 2πr ÷ v = (2 × π × 7 000 000) ÷ 7500 = 5860 s (~98 min)

slides.title: Geostationary satellites
slides.oldHtml:
Geostationary satellites

Challenge
A geostationary satellite orbits once every 24 hours at height 35 000 km above Earth’s surface (Earth’s radius = 6400 km). Find its speed in m/s.
Watch the exam trap: r is from Earth’s centre!
  • r = 6400 + 35 000 = 41 400 km = 41 400 000 m
  • T = 24 × 3600 = 86 400 s
v = 2π × 41 400 000 ÷ 86 400 = 3010 m/s
slides.newHtml:
